# Repository Guidelines

Velociraptor (v10r) is a SvelteKit pattern library for adaptation. Claude Code follows
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

## Project Structure

- `src/routes/`: localized pages under `[[locale=locale]]/`; REST/SSE under `api/`.
- `src/lib/components/`: reusable UI; `src/lib/state/`: shared rune state.
- `src/lib/server/`: domains, database schemas/access, and integrations.
- `static/`: assets; `content/`: authored content; `messages/`: translations.
- `pattern-library/`: canonical registry; `mcp/`: stdio transport; `scripts/`: tooling.

## Development and Validation

Claude Code cloud sessions are the default place to develop: no container, no secrets,
commands run directly (`bun run validate`). Local sessions run tooling inside the `v10r`
Podman container. What runs where, and what to report as not run:
[development-environment.md](docs/foundation/development-environment.md).
Never run package managers on the host; keep `package.json` and `bun.lock` synchronized.

```bash
bun run validate                     # authoritative gate (cloud)
bun run validate:build               # + production build and perf ratchet
podman compose up -d                 # local: start development on :5173
podman exec v10r bun run validate    # local: the same gate in the container
```

The gate includes typechecking, Biome, tests, registry/excerpts, i18n/content, and quality
checks. No CI pipeline exists. Report failures accurately.

## Architecture and Coding Style

Keep domains framework-free; adapters own HTTP responses, redirects, and date
serialization. Never import `#lib/server/` into `.svelte` or universal `+page.ts`.
Change code directly: no compatibility layers, migration shims, or deprecation paths.

Follow `biome.json`: tabs, LF, 120-column width, single JS quotes, semicolons, trailing
commas. Use PascalCase components, kebab-case modules, and `.svelte.ts` for runes.
Consult [docs/naming.md](docs/naming.md) before introducing names; comments explain why —
the principle behind both is [docs/foundation/self-expressive-project.md](docs/foundation/self-expressive-project.md).
Never name a prop `state`.

Use existing components instead of raw buttons, inputs, selects, or textareas.
Exceptions: hidden inputs, table-row checkboxes, numeric selects, and specially styled
interactive regions. Colors use `src/app.css` tokens.

## Testing

Co-locate Vitest `*.test.ts`; database tests use `*.pglite.test.ts` and PGlite.
Run one file with `bunx vitest run <path>` (locally: `podman exec v10r bunx vitest run <path>`).
MCP uses `bun:test` (`test:mcp`). Test invariants, security, and regressions; verify UI
through browser showcases. No coverage threshold is configured.

## Documentation and Generated Files

Start at [docs/README.md](docs/README.md); navigate directory READMEs before topics.
Never grep blindly through `docs/`. Read `docs/codebase-organization.md` and
`docs/system-abstraction.md` for architecture. Reference canonical sources; avoid duplicate
stack documentation.

Never hand-edit generated pattern pages, Paraglide output, MCP excerpts, or retrieval
indexes. Use `package.json` generators; `refresh` also ingests docs into
the database. See [mcp/README.md](mcp/README.md) for machine-readable access.

## Commits and Branches

History mixes informal subjects with `feat(scope):` and `refactor(scope):`; prefer
descriptive subjects that explain behavior.

Work on a feature branch: commit and push it, hand off the branch and its HEAD SHA, and stop.
No PR is needed; a PR is only the fallback vehicle of a ship. GitHub `main` moves only when
ApeDevil explicitly says to ship in the conversation — then follow
[shipping.md](docs/stack/ops/shipping.md) (squash into `main` → GitLab sync → Vercel). Never push
`main` or GitLab, never force-push, stash, or reset. Run a `vr` command only when
specifically requested.

Name every branch you create `<agent>/<env>/<feature>`: `<agent>` is `claude` or `codex`; `<env>` is `cloud` in a cloud environment (Claude: `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`; Codex: no `~/.codex/` directory), otherwise `local`; `<feature>` is short kebab-case. Example: `claude/local/add-login-page`. Rename an auto-named branch (`claude/brave-bohr-9jw2fq`) to this form before its first push.

# Asset Production

A structured, validated request becomes a checked 3D asset: parametric geometry built in
code, inspected, written as GLB with its provenance inside, measured, optionally kept in a
write-once store, and loaded into the existing Threlte viewer. One engine, one job shape, three
callers (HTTP, CLI, MCP tool). Pattern record: `asset-production-pipeline`.

## Contents

- [Why this shape](#why-this-shape) - the concerns kept apart
- [Engine choice](#engine-choice) - what was compared, and why plain TypeScript won
- [The pipeline](#the-pipeline) - request → check → generate → inspect → encode → verify → keep
- [Invariants](#invariants) - what holds, and which test holds it
- [Quality gates](#quality-gates) - what every exported asset must pass
- [Execution environments](#execution-environments) - in-process and isolated worker; GPU not built
- [Security and reliability](#security-and-reliability) - untrusted input, limits, no overwrite
- [AI and MCP](#ai-and-mcp) - typed operations, never code
- [Measurements](#measurements) - real numbers, where they come from
- [Showcase](#showcase) - `/showcases/3d/produce`
- [Toward a managed service](#toward-a-managed-service) - proposals, not built
- [Anti-patterns](#anti-patterns)
- [Proof](#proof) - the tests and pages behind the record
- [Emulating it](#emulating-it)

## Why this shape

"Generate a model" tends to become one function that reads form fields, builds meshes, calls an
exporter, writes a file and returns a URL. Each concern then blocks the others: the exporter
cannot be swapped, the job cannot move to a worker, an AI cannot call it safely, and nobody can
say which code made a file. This pattern keeps ten things apart:

| Concern | Lives in | Knows nothing about |
|---|---|---|
| Request schema — the only way to ask | `src/lib/schemas/asset-production.ts` | how geometry is made |
| Generator — parameters → mesh, deterministic | `src/lib/asset-production/generators/` | GLB, storage, HTTP |
| Mesh intermediate — primitives, shells, envelope | `src/lib/asset-production/mesh.ts` | which generator or engine made it |
| Inspection and gates | `inspect.ts`, `glb.ts` (`readGlb`), `engine.ts` | the request's meaning |
| Engine adapter — stages, budget, cancellation | `engine.ts` (`AssetProductionEngine`) | where it runs |
| Execution environment | `src/lib/server/asset-production/{in-process,isolated-process}.ts` | the geometry |
| Output artifact — byte-stable GLB with `asset.extras` | `glb.ts` (`encodeGlb`) | the store |
| Storage adapter — write-once, owner-scoped | `store.ts` (`AssetStore`) | how assets are made |
| Job lifecycle and report | `job.ts`, `run-job.ts`, `src/lib/asset-production/report.ts` | the transport |
| Provenance and measurements | `derivation.ts`, the report | the viewer |
| Viewer / presentation | `src/routes/…/showcases/3d/produce/` | how the GLB was made |

The core (`src/lib/asset-production/`) imports only its schema, Valibot and Three.js's
`Vector3`: no Svelte, no DOM, no Node API. The same engine runs in a serverless function, a
child process, a terminal and a browser — the showcase uses it client-side for the live
estimate and the parameter rules before it sends anything.

Vocabulary: **asset production** — always qualified, because bare `production` is the deployed
environment. `AssetRequest`, `AssetGenerator`, `AssetProductionEngine`, `EngineRun`,
`AssetExecutionEnvironment`, `AssetJob`, `AssetReport`, `AssetStore`. See `docs/naming.md`.

## Engine choice

Decision principle: the simplest engine that meets the initial requirements — parametric,
deterministic, GLB out, cheap to run, no new infrastructure. Compared against those, not
against feature lists.

| Option | Headless + scriptable | GLB out | Footprint | Determinism | Runs on Vercel / in the browser | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Plain TypeScript** (Three.js math + own builders + own GLB writer) | yes | yes, own writer (~200 lines) | 0 new runtime deps (Three.js is already shipped) | byte-identical across Bun (JSC) and Node (V8) — measured | yes / yes | **chosen** |
| A′. Three.js `GLTFExporter` | yes | yes | in repo | — | needs `Blob`/`FileReader`; not DOM-free on the server | rejected: the DOM dependency is the problem the writer removes |
| A″. CSG in JS (`manifold-3d` WASM 2.8 MB unpacked, `three-bvh-csg`, `@jscad/modeling` 1.6 MB) | yes | via a writer | +1 dep each | manifold: deterministic | yes / yes | not needed yet: overlapping closed shells render correctly; add **manifold-3d** when a target needs one booleaned solid (3D printing, volume) |
| A‴. OpenCascade (`replicad` 6.8 MB, `opencascade.js` 67 MB unpacked) | yes | via STEP/STL → convert | heavy WASM | B-rep kernel | serverless cold start suffers | only for true CAD (fillets, STEP exchange) |
| **B. OpenSCAD** | yes (CLI) | no native glTF: STL/OFF/AMF/3MF, then a converter | native binary (tens of MB) + container | the Manifold backend is fast; CGAL is slow | no — needs a container worker | rejected now: a second language, a container, and a conversion step for no capability this slice needs |
| **C. Blender** (`blender -b --python`, or `bpy` from PyPI) | yes | yes (built-in exporter) | several hundred MB; Python pinned to Blender's | add-on and version-dependent | no — a container worker, ideally per job | rejected now; it is the right tool for **conversion, retopology, baking, rendering previews** of imported assets — see below |
| D. Server-side CAD APIs (Onshape, APS) | yes | yes | paid API, network | vendor's | no | rejected: paid, external, not portable |

Footprints for B and C are from the projects' published distributions, not measured in this
repository; the npm sizes are `npm view <pkg> dist.unpackedSize` on 2026-10-29.

**When Blender earns its place.** When a demonstrated requirement needs what only a DCC tool
does — importing arbitrary user files (FBX, OBJ, USD), decimation, UV unwrapping, baking,
thumbnails rendered with Cycles. Then: a separate CPU container worker (`--network=none`,
memory and CPU caps, read-only image, scratch volume), driven by a **closed list of typed
operations** that map to fixed, versioned Python scripts in the image. Never `--python-expr`
with caller text, never an MCP tool that forwards Python, never add-ons installed at run time.
It slots in as another `AssetExecutionEnvironment` plus an engine adapter; the request schema,
report, store and viewer stay.

## The pipeline

```
AssetRequest (untrusted JSON)
  └─ check     strict Valibot parse · cross-parameter rules · exact estimate vs budget
  └─ generate  generator(parameters, checkpoint) → GeneratedMesh { primitives, envelope }
  └─ inspect   counts · bounds · closed + outward shells · finite · unit normals · envelope
  └─ encode    byte-stable GLB · asset.extras.v10r = { transform, requestDigest, derivationKey }
  └─ verify    read the GLB back · byte budget
  └─ keep?     AssetStore.put(owner/derivationKey) — created | reused | conflict
  └─ AssetReport { output, derivation, engine, generator, environment, inspection,
                   diagnostics, measurements, provenance (PROV-DM) }
```

Stages are timed separately. A refused request never reaches `generate`; a failed one never
returns bytes. Findings are `AssetDiagnostic`s with a fixed severity per code
(`diagnostics.ts`), never exceptions.

The demonstration generator is a **structural ring**: a square-section truss bent into a ring
(Warren, single-direction or X bracing), spokes to a capped hub with docking ports, and boxed
modules on the outer chords. Nine bounded numeric parameters and one pick list; from 1,248 to
68,352 triangles. Every strut is a capped tube, every module a box: each is a closed shell.

**Derivation and provenance.** The derivation key is the repository's `derivationKey`
(`src/lib/server/db/content-hash.ts`) over `procedural-ts@1/structural-ring@1` and the request's
canonical JSON (sorted keys, label excluded — it is presentation). Same key ⇒ same bytes; that
is what makes a repeat run a cache hit and a byte mismatch a loud `store.conflict`. The report's
`provenance` is the PROV-DM core of `docs/blueprint/integrity/derivation.md`: the entity
(sha256), the activity (transform, start, end), the agent (`human` / `software` / `ai`, with
`onBehalfOf`) — never an IP or an email.

## Invariants

| # | Invariant | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The core imports no framework, DOM or runtime API | the boundary gate in `engine.test.ts` |
| 2 | Untrusted input is refused before any geometry is built: unknown keys, unknown generators, strings for numbers, NaN, ±Infinity, out-of-range values, cross-parameter conflicts, over-budget estimates | `engine.test.ts` (16 refusal cases) |
| 3 | The budget is checked from an exact estimate before building and from the real mesh after | `engine.test.ts` (estimate = actual at the bounds) |
| 4 | Deterministic: the same request gives the same bytes, in-process and in a worker, on V8 and on JSC | `engine.test.ts`, `isolated-process.test.ts` |
| 5 | Every exported file passes the Khronos glTF validator with no error or warning, and loads in Three.js `GLTFLoader` | `glb.test.ts` |
| 6 | A damaged GLB is refused by the read-back gate | `glb.test.ts` |
| 7 | Cancellation and deadlines stop a run and keep nothing; an isolated worker is killed, never orphaned | `engine.test.ts`, `isolated-process.test.ts` |
| 8 | The store never overwrites: repeat = reuse, mismatch = conflict with the kept asset untouched; keys cannot leave their owner | `run-job.test.ts` |
| 9 | A job never publishes: kept assets are owner-scoped drafts | `run-job.test.ts`, `tools.test.ts` |
| 10 | An agent can ask only for typed operations; code, unknown tools and unknown generators are refused | `tools.test.ts` |

## Quality gates

| Gate | Where | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Strict schema, bounded numbers, integer fields | `check` | error `request.invalid` |
| Cross-parameter rules (one spoke, hub through the truss, members thicker than the section, bays shorter than members, more modules than bays) | generator `check` | error `parameter.conflict` |
| Triangle and vertex budget, from the estimate | `check` | error `budget.*` |
| Finite positions and normals; indices in range; no zero-area triangle | `inspect` | error |
| Every shell closed (each welded edge used exactly twice) and outward (positive signed volume) | `inspect` | error `mesh.open-shell` / `mesh.inverted-shell` |
| Inside the envelope the generator declared from its parameters | `inspect` | error `mesh.outside-envelope` |
| Normals unit length; estimate equals what was built | `inspect` | warning |
| GLB framing, JSON, bufferViews, accessors, POSITION min/max, indices — read back | `verify` | error `glb.malformed` |
| GLB byte budget | `verify` | error `budget.bytes` |
| Khronos validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings | tests (`gltf-validator`, dev only) | — |

"Closed" is per shell. Overlapping struts are separate closed shells, not one booleaned solid:
right for rendering, not for 3D printing (add a CSG union first).

## Execution environments

| Environment | Isolation | Stops by | Built |
|---|---|---|---|
| `in-process` (the HTTP function, the CLI default) | none beyond the budget | cooperative checkpoints (per bay, per stage) against the deadline and `AbortSignal` | yes |
| `isolated-process` (`createIsolatedProcessEnvironment`, CLI `--isolated`) | own process and heap, env stripped to `PATH`, capped stdout | SIGKILL at the deadline, on cancel, or past the output cap; exit awaited | yes |
| CPU container worker | + `--network=none --memory --cpus --read-only` | same protocol as the isolated worker (`scripts/asset-production/worker.ts` is the entrypoint) | no — documented |
| GPU worker | — | — | no: no operation here needs a GPU |

## Security and reliability

- **Inputs are untrusted.** Strict objects, closed numeric ranges, a discriminated generator id.
  The request cannot name a file, a script, a URL or an engine flag. Bodies over 4 KiB are
  refused before parsing; the HTTP route rate-limits per IP before any geometry (20 / minute).
- **Work is bounded before it starts.** The estimate is exact, so an oversized request costs
  one arithmetic pass. Inside a run the deadline is carved from the request's own `Deadline`.
- **No uncontrolled processes.** The isolated worker is killed with SIGKILL at its deadline and
  its exit is awaited before the job resolves.
- **No overwrite, no publish.** Write-once by derivation key; a directory store writes to a
  staging directory renamed into place in one step; keys are `[a-z0-9-]` segments resolved
  under the root. A kept asset is a draft; publishing is a separate, explicit act (not built).
- **Imported assets.** This slice imports none. A future import path reads GLB with the same
  `readGlb` gate first, in the isolated environment, with the same byte budget.
- **Privacy.** The showcase stores nothing and reports no identity; the agent is "showcase
  visitor".

## AI and MCP

`createAssetToolRegistry()` is a `ToolRegistry` for the hosted MCP transport with two tools:
`describe_asset_generators` (parameters, bounds, budget) and `produce_asset` (the request schema
as its JSON Schema input; returns the report as text and keeps an owner-scoped draft). An agent
creates a variation by changing typed parameters, reads the findings, and tries again — the same
propose → check → revise loop as the PIM transform recipe, with no free-form code anywhere.

It is **not mounted** on the public `/api/mcp` endpoint, by decision: `produce_asset` spends
CPU per call, and anonymous compute belongs behind the showcase route's rate limit. Mount it on
an authenticated endpoint (admin, or per-user with a quota) — one registry line. No AI provider
is involved anywhere; everything works without one.

## Measurements

`bun run asset:bench --runs 20`, 2026-10-29, cloud container: Intel Xeon @ 2.80 GHz, 4 vCPUs,
Linux x64. p50 / p95 over 20 in-process runs (5 isolated), first run included. Node 22.22
(what Vercel runs) via `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/asset-production/bench.ts`:

| Case | Triangles | GLB | In-process total p50 / p95 | CPU p50 | Isolated worker total p50 | Same bytes every run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| minimal (8 bays, 3 facets) | 1,248 | 43 KiB | 10.2 / 22.7 ms | 7.4 ms | 119 ms | yes |
| default (24 bays) | 9,800 | 306 KiB | 18.6 / 26.1 ms | 15.7 ms | 153 ms | yes |
| largest in bounds | 68,352 | 2,457 KiB | 71.0 / 104.4 ms | 85.8 ms | 315 ms | yes |

Under Bun 1.3.12 the in-process totals are 10.3 / 24.4 / 103.8 ms. Largest-case stage split on
Node: generate 22 ms, inspect 34 ms, encode 3 ms, verify 2 ms. Inspection dominates; it is the
price of the shell check. The isolated worker adds ~100–150 ms of process start and module load
per run (its RSS after a run: 67–130 MiB).

What this implies, not measured on Vercel: the largest request is ~0.1 s of CPU in a function,
so the showcase is cheap per run; the cost risk is volume, which the rate limit bounds. The GLB
travels base64 in JSON — 2.5 MB becomes ~3.3 MB, under Vercel's 4.5 MB response cap. Browser
parse and paint times are shown live on the page; they are not quoted here because they depend
on the visitor's device. Browsers: anything that runs the existing Threlte showcases (WebGL 2);
without WebGL the page still produces the asset and shows its report.

## Showcase

`/showcases/3d/produce`: presets (outpost, default, station), a slider per parameter and the
bracing pick list, a live estimate and the parameter rules computed in the browser by the same
core, Generate / Cancel, the model in a Threlte canvas (on-demand rendering, studio light,
`<svelte:boundary>` fallback), and four panels — validation (every gate, or every finding),
output (size, counts, shells, extent, sha256, derivation key, download GLB and report), engine
(engine, generator, environment, runtime, budget), measurements (server stages and CPU, round
trip, browser parse, time to paint).

## Toward a managed service

Proposals — none of this is built, and none needs a paid provider for the slice above.

| Need | Extension point | Reuse |
|---|---|---|
| Queued, user-scoped jobs | persist `AssetJob` rows; claim with a lease | `durable-step-execution` |
| Scheduling, retries, sweeping stale jobs | a job slug | `jobs-scheduler` |
| Persistent project storage | an `AssetStore` on R2 with `If-None-Match: *` puts | `databases-object-storage` (`#lib/server/store`) |
| Bounded CPU / memory / disk | the isolated worker in a container with limits | `architecture-external-service` |
| Quotas and cost accounting | per-owner triangle·seconds from `measurements`, checked before `check` | `anti-abuse-ai-budget` |
| Approval for expensive runs | estimate → proposal → approve → run | `deskbot-approval-gate` |
| Cancellation of queued jobs | `queued → cancelled`; running → kill the worker | `job.ts` moves |
| GPU work (baking, rendering) | another environment + a Blender adapter with typed operations | above |

## Anti-patterns

- **Unrestricted engine scripting** — a tool or form field that forwards Python or OpenSCAD
  source. Typed operations only.
- **A heavy engine for light geometry** — Blender or a CAD kernel for meshes plain code builds
  in milliseconds.
- **Exporting from the scene graph** — `GLTFExporter` in the server drags the DOM in and makes
  bytes depend on renderer state.
- **Trusting the estimate alone** — the budget is checked again on what was really built.
- **Overwriting by name** — `ring.glb` replaced in place. Key by derivation, write once.
- **Timestamps in the asset** — they break byte identity; times belong in the report.
- **Publishing from the job** — a job produces a draft; publishing is the owner's act.
- **Claiming structural validity** — the gates check the file and its surfaces, never strength.

## Proof

| Surface | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/asset-production/engine.test.ts` | the pipeline, determinism, exact estimates, 16 refusals, cancellation and deadline, the boundary gate |
| `src/lib/asset-production/glb.test.ts` | Khronos validator clean (16- and 32-bit indices), `GLTFLoader` loads it, damaged files refused |
| `src/lib/asset-production/inspect.test.ts` | every inspection finding on a crafted defect |
| `src/lib/server/asset-production/run-job.test.ts` | report, provenance, label-independent derivation, write-once memory and directory stores, lifecycle |
| `src/lib/server/asset-production/isolated-process.test.ts` | same bytes on Bun and Node; kill at deadline, on cancel, past the output cap; failed start |
| `src/lib/server/asset-production/tools.test.ts` | the MCP registry: schema, describe, produce a draft, refuse code / unknown generator / over budget / unknown tool |
| `/showcases/3d/produce` | the live slice, generation to presentation |
| `tests/browser/produce.spec.ts` | Playwright: the page generates, shows the model and the report, refuses a conflict (`bun run test:browser`) |
| `bun run asset:produce`, `bun run asset:bench` | the CLI with the directory store; the measurements above |

## Emulating it

1. Write the request schema first: a discriminated generator id, strict objects, closed ranges
   from one bounds table your UI and tool description also read.
2. Write the generator against a mesh intermediate with shells and a declared envelope, plus an
   exact `estimate`. Test estimate = actual at every bound.
3. Add inspection and a DOM-free, byte-stable GLB writer with a read-back gate; run the Khronos
   validator in tests.
4. Wrap it in an engine with timed stages, a budget checked twice and checkpoints.
5. Put the job, report, derivation key and write-once store around it; then the callers (route
   with a rate limit, CLI, MCP registry).
6. Present last: the viewer loads the GLB the job returned, nothing else.

# Product Composition

Typed, reusable 3D products with connection ports, joined into an editable assembly: a
heating system of boiler, pump and radiators, or a shelf of uprights and boards. One engine,
no domain inside it. Pattern record: `product-connection-engine`.

## Contents

- [Why this shape](#why-this-shape) - the layers kept apart
- [Vocabulary](#vocabulary) - the names, and the ones avoided
- [Document and frames](#document-and-frames) - schema, port frames, IFC mapping
- [Invariants](#invariants) - what holds, and which test holds it
- [Operations and diagnostics](#operations-and-diagnostics) - pure edits, findings as data
- [Rendering and editing](#rendering-and-editing) - the Threlte layer
- [Plausibility, not certification](#plausibility-not-certification) - the safety line
- [Honest scope](#honest-scope) - what it does not do
- [Routing: evaluated, not built](#routing-evaluated-not-built) - when auto-routing earns its place
- [Seams outside the core](#seams-outside-the-core) - storage, IFC, telemetry, simulation
- [Proof](#proof) - the tests and pages behind the record
- [Emulating it](#emulating-it) - six steps, core first

## Why this shape

A configurator that draws products and lets the user join them tends to grow one tangled
component: meshes know about pipes, pipes know about thread sizes, and saving means
serialising the scene graph. This pattern keeps seven things apart, so each can change alone:

| Layer | Lives in | Knows nothing about |
|---|---|---|
| Definition — a catalogue entry: geometry, ports, internal passages | the document | where it is placed |
| Occurrence — one placed use of a definition | the document | the other products |
| Port — a typed connection point with a frame | the definition | what it is joined to |
| Coupling — *which* two ports are joined, mated or by a conduit | the document | the geometry between them |
| Conduit — *where* the pipe or cable runs (waypoints) | the document | why the ports are compatible |
| Rules — which ports may join | a `PortStandardRegistry` the caller supplies | heating, shelving, any domain |
| Rendering — meshes, markers, tubes, gizmo | `#lib/components/3d/composition/` | the rules |

Topology is not geometry: IFC 4.3 makes the same split between `IfcRelConnectsPorts` and the
element that realises it. The core (`#lib/product-composition/`) imports no Svelte, `$app`,
DOM or WebGL object, so an import, an AI tool or a server write can validate a document
exactly as the editor does.

## Vocabulary

`ProductComposition`, `ProductDefinition`, `ProductOccurrence`, `ProductPort`,
`PortStandard` / `PortStandardRegistry`, `Coupling` (`mated` | `conduit`), `Conduit`,
`passages`, `exposedPorts`, `PortNetwork`, `CompositionDiagnostic`. Each term, and the words
rejected for it, is a row in [`docs/naming.md`](../../naming.md).

## Document and frames

Schema: `src/lib/schemas/product-composition.ts` (strict Valibot objects).

```
ProductComposition { format: 1, id, label?, definitions, occurrences, couplings, conduits }
ProductDefinition  { id, label, body, metadata? }
  body: { kind: 'geometry', geometry, ports, passages? }
      | { kind: 'composition', occurrences, couplings, conduits, exposedPorts }
ProductPort        { id, label, standard, direction, gender, frame, capacity?, parameters? }
PortStandard       { id, family, label, genders, directions, clocking, matchParameters }
Coupling           { id, a, b, mode }        // a and b unordered
Conduit            { id, coupling, waypoints } // interior points only
```

- **The document is self-contained.** It carries every definition it uses. The registry of
  port standards is supplied by the caller. "Versioned" means `format`; versioning
  definitions belongs to a storage adapter.
- **Port frame.** +Z points out of the product, +Y is the clocking reference. A mate is a
  half turn about +Y: the two +Z axes face each other and the +Y axes line up.
- **IFC 4.3 mapping.** An `IfcDistributionPort` Axis points out for a SOURCE port and in for
  a SINK, and rigidly joined ports carry equal frames. Ours always points out (as SolidWorks
  Routing and Onshape mate connectors do): IFC Axis = our +Z for a source, −Z for a sink.
- **Semantics.** `direction` is the nominal design direction; actual flow is never
  computed. `neutral` gender is genderless (flanges, hermaphroditic connectors). Matching is
  equality on `matchParameters` only — keying such as an IEC 60309 clock position is a match
  parameter; ratings stay informational.
- **Determinism.** Every number is quantised to 1e-9 before it enters the document, and a
  quaternion's sign is fixed *after* quantising, so a half turn always serialises the same
  way. `stringifyComposition` sorts keyed collections and passages: the same edits give the
  same bytes.

## Invariants

| # | Invariant | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The core is framework-free and renderer-free: only its schema, Valibot and Three.js math classes | the boundary gate in `compose.test.ts` |
| 2 | Pure and deterministic: same operations → byte-identical document, ±π included | `frame.test.ts`, `serialize.test.ts` |
| 3 | Couplings are well-formed: no self-coupling, no duplicate pair, capacity respected (a mate is exclusive), exposed ports never share an inner port | `validate.test.ts`, `operations.test.ts` |
| 4 | Compatibility comes from registry data only; the core names no domain | `standards.test.ts`; the neutrality gate in `compose.test.ts` |
| 5 | Mates hold within 1e-6: a connect snaps the moving side's whole cluster, a move re-derives the cluster along a spanning tree (no drift), consistent rings are allowed | `operations.test.ts`, `frame.test.ts` |
| 6 | Conduit ends always derive from the live port frames | `conduit.test.ts` |
| 7 | Removing an occurrence removes its couplings and their conduits | `operations.test.ts` |
| 8 | Findings are data, never throws; parse is fail-closed | `validate.test.ts`, `serialize.test.ts` |

Nested bodies are read-only from the outer level: no operation edits inside a definition.
Resolution and networks work on the flattened graph, so passages through a subassembly count.

## Operations and diagnostics

Every operation in `operations.ts` takes a composition and returns
`OperationResult { composition, diagnostics }`. A refused operation returns its input
unchanged with the reasons. Ids come from the caller or `nextId(prefix, existing)` — no
`Math.random`, no `Date`.

| Operation | Notes |
|---|---|
| `addOccurrence`, `removeOccurrence` | add copies a missing definition (and its nested ones) from a catalogue; remove cascades |
| `moveOccurrence`, `rotateOccurrence` | the mated cluster follows |
| `connect`, `disconnect` | connect runs the same checks validation does, for that one coupling |
| `setConduitWaypoints`, `insertWaypoint`, `removeWaypoint` | refused on a mated coupling |

`validateComposition` returns findings sorted by `(code, subject)`. Severity is fixed per
code (`diagnostics.ts`):

| Group | Codes | Severity | Raised by |
|---|---|---|---|
| definition | `definition.missing`, `composition.recursive` | error | validation |
| coupling | `coupling.unresolved`, `coupling.self`, `coupling.duplicate` | error | validation |
| port | `port.incompatible` (with its mismatch list), `port.capacity` | error | validation |
| port | `port.open` | info | validation |
| mate | `mate.misaligned` | error | validation |
| conduit | `conduit.unresolved`, `conduit.mode`, `conduit.duplicate` | error | validation |
| passage | `passage.unresolved`, `passage.self` | error | validation |
| exposed port | `exposed-port.unresolved`, `exposed-port.shared` | error | validation |
| operation | `id.duplicate`, `occurrence.unresolved`, `waypoint.unresolved` | error | refused operation only |

## Rendering and editing

`#lib/components/3d/composition/` reads only the core's resolved output:

- `CompositionCanvas` — `<svelte:boundary>` fallback around an on-demand `<Canvas>`, exposed
  as `role="img"` with a label that points to the keyboard way.
- `CompositionScene` — products, port markers (a larger invisible hit proxy for touch),
  conduit tubes (a `CurvePath` of straight runs with a quadratic fillet per corner, the old
  geometry disposed on rebuild), waypoint handles, and a translate-only `TransformControls`.
- `CompositionEditor` (`composition-editor.svelte.ts`) — `$state.raw` document, selection,
  an undo stack of snapshots (100, no redo), drag gestures that commit one undo step, dry-run
  coupling options, JSON import and export.

Two things the installed Threlte does not do for you: `@threlte/extras` 9.7.1's
`TransformControls` does not pause `CameraControls`, so the scene
toggles `controls.enabled` on drag start and end; and on-demand rendering needs an explicit
`invalidate()` whenever the document, selection or theme changes.

Colours are tokens: product tones map to theme tokens, port families to `--chart-N` by
their sorted position, which keeps the renderer as domain-free as the core. Physical tones
(`enamel`, `copper`, `brass`, `chrome`, `steel`, `glass`, `rubber`) map to the `--scene-*`
tokens, which keep their colour in every theme.

Surfaces are roles too. A primitive's optional `finish` (`matte`, `satin`, `gloss`, `metal`,
`brushed`) resolves in `surface-finish.ts` to physically based material parameters and
procedural grey maps (tileable value noise in `DataTexture`s: no download, no DOM, same pixels
every time); a box may round its edges (`radius`), and `torus` joins box, cylinder and sphere.
`primitive-geometry.ts` shares one geometry per distinct shape across occurrences.

Light and setting are the renderer's, never the document's: a generated studio environment
(`RoomEnvironment` through PMREM), a shadow-casting key light aimed at the composition,
Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping. A caller may pass a `RoomLayout` — floor, back wall, corner,
windows, plaster and tile, a night palette in the dark theme — so wall-hung products read as
hung; with walls, the camera stays in front of them. `conduitSurfaces` draws a port family's
conduits as a physical run (copper pipe, a slim cable) and keeps the family colour on the
fittings at each end.

Everything the canvas does has a keyboard path in the showcase's inspector: a products list,
each product's ports, a picker of compatible partners, nudge and turn buttons, a waypoint
list. A status region announces each success and refusal.

## Plausibility, not certification

Every verdict means "the declared data fits": thread sizes agree, a mate lines up, a port is
not over-used. Nothing sizes a pipe, rates a cable, checks a pressure or approves an
installation. The showcase keeps a warning banner on screen that says so, and no copy,
diagnostic or record may claim engineering or electrical validity. This rule is held by
review, not by a test.

## Honest scope

- No constraint solver: mates and port rules only. The editor rotates in steps.
- Ratings (`capacity` aside) are informational; there are no range checks.
- No collision detection between products or conduits.

## Routing: evaluated, not built

Conduits are routed by hand: interior waypoints between two port stubs (`CONDUIT_STUB`,
0.1 m along each port's +Z). Auto-routing was evaluated and left out of the core. The
baseline when it is needed is bend-penalised A* on a voxel grid around the products, run as
a separate operation that writes waypoints. Build it when a document has obstacles that
matter, more than about ten conduits, or a catalogue of fittings to route through.

## Seams outside the core

Each is a caller of the core, not a part of it:

- **Storage** — persisting documents and versioning definitions.
- **IFC / BIM** — import and export through the frame mapping above.
- **Telemetry** — live values bound to occurrences or ports by id.
- **Simulation and sizing** — flows, pressures, loads; engineering tools own these.
- **Auto-routing** — see above.

## Proof

| Surface | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/product-composition/*.test.ts` (8 files) | frames, standards, serialisation, resolution, networks, validation, operations, conduits |
| `src/lib/showcases/3d/compose/compose.test.ts` | both fixtures valid; the core names no domain and imports no framework; a six-step scenario replayed on the core |
| `src/lib/components/3d/composition/{conduit-tube,composition-editor.svelte}.test.ts` | tube geometry; undo, gestures, import |
| `/showcases/3d/compose` | heating (subassembly, conduits, open ports) and shelving (a ring of mates, GLB sofas) on one engine |
| `tests/browser/compose.spec.ts` | the scenario by keyboard and a gizmo drag, in Chromium (`bun run test:browser`, outside `validate`) |

## Emulating it

1. Copy the schema and `frame.ts` first; agree the port frame convention before any geometry.
2. Define your `PortStandard`s as data — never as `if (thread)` in the core.
3. Port `serialize.ts` and its canonical sort, then the operations with `OperationResult`.
4. Add `validate.ts` and the domain-neutrality gate with your own domain's words.
5. Write the scenario test on the core before any UI.
6. Add rendering last, reading only resolved output; give every canvas action a keyboard path.

# AI Blueprint

Architecture and implementation designs for the AI subsystem.

## Overview

Multi-provider chat assistant with tool calling, Graph RAG retrieval, catalog grounding, and desk integration, plus a vision capability for image metadata extraction. Uses Vercel AI SDK 7 for a unified API across providers ([ai-sdk-v7.md](./ai-sdk-v7.md)).

### Provider connections and the registry

Providers are connected by the administrator under **Admin → AI → Models** — enable, model id,
API key (stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted under `ENCRYPTION_KEY`), project default, connection test.
Nothing is read from `.env`. Every AI operation loads the saved connections at its start
(`loadProviderRegistry()`) and resolves against that snapshot, so a save reaches the next
request on every instance. Full design: [provider-routing.md](./provider-routing.md#provider-connections).

Three resolvers handle different jobs, each over the loaded registry:

| Resolver | Purpose | Order |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `resolveActiveProvider` | Chat-only turns (no tools) | user pref → project default → first connected |
| `resolveToolProvider` | Tool-calling turns | user pref → project default → OpenAI → Google → others |
| `resolveVisionProvider` | Image input (vision) | user pref → project default → Google → OpenAI |

Capabilities are derived from the saved **model id** (`model-capabilities.ts`), not the vendor; an
unrecognized model is treated as text-only. Groq/llama carries the tools flag but probabilistically
emits tool calls as plain text rather than a structured `tool_calls` field. The `tool-leak-guard.ts`
transform suppresses that markup so the turn degrades to empty instead of leaking syntax. For
reliable grounding, the tool provider prefers OpenAI → Google.

| Provider | Suggested model | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|
| Groq | openai/gpt-oss-120b | Tool-capable; text-only (no vision); llama-3.x also recognized |
| OpenAI | gpt-4o-mini | Preferred tool provider; vision-capable |
| Google Gemini | gemini-2.5-flash | Second-choice tool provider; preferred vision provider; its key also serves embeddings |

Circuit breaker: 60s cooldown on rate-limited providers (`markCooldown` / `isCooledDown`), Redis-backed so it is cross-instance and async.

## Key Modules

Two per-surface routes (`/api/ai/chatbot`, `/api/ai/deskbot`) replace the former single `/api/ai/chat`; each sets the `surface` discriminant explicitly and shares one entry guard. `chat-orchestrator.ts` remains the single dispatcher. See [surfaces.md](./surfaces.md).

| Provider resolvers | `src/lib/server/ai/providers.ts` | Chat/tool/vision resolution over a loaded registry, cooldowns, user preferences |
| Image metadata domain | `src/lib/server/imagemeta/` | Framework-free core: ingest, EXIF-strip, vision extract, persist |

```

                                                  │  (one orchestrator; surface = explicit dispatch discriminant)
                                                  ├── registry from guardAiRequest (loadProviderRegistry) → resolveActiveProvider / resolveToolProvider
                                                  ├── fallback rotation on rate limit (per-surface)
                                                  ├── chatbot: corpus map + relevance-gated docs grounding + catalog

```

# Agent actions

How one assistant turn acts on both sides of the wire — server tools on stored data, client
actions on the interface in front of the user — through one contract, one catalogue and one
orchestrator. This file is the decision record and the pattern; the code is the contract.

## Agent action architecture

**Problem.** The deskbot could read and change the user's files, but it could not touch the
workspace the user is looking at. "Open my architecture document on the right" needs a server
read (find the file, as this user) and then an operation that only exists in the browser (a
panel in a dock). The obvious additions — a second registry for "UI actions", a channel that
pushes commands to browsers, a store of pending requests — each duplicate something the turn
already has, and each is a new place where an agent can claim work it did not do or reach a
write it was never approved for.

**Method.** An *agent action* is anything the model may ask the application to do. All of them
are entries of the one tool catalogue, `TOOL_MANIFEST` (`#lib/types/ai-tools.ts`); what differs
is declared per entry, on two independent axes:

| Axis | Values | Decides |
|---|---|---|
| `risk` — what it changes | `read` · `view` · `create` · `write` · `destructive` | Whether a human approves first (`requiresApproval(risk)`: write and destructive) |
| `executor` — where it runs | `server` · `client` | Who produces the result, and therefore how far the result is believed |

A **client action** is a tool with `executor: 'client'`. It has no server `execute`. The model
calls it like any tool; the call travels in the turn's own response stream to the browser that
sent the turn; a registered handler there validates the input, acts, reads the interface back
and answers with a bounded `ClientActionResult`; the browser sends the thread back and the same
turn continues. `view` is the risk that makes this safe to run unattended: it changes what is
shown, never what is stored.

```
user message ──► POST /api/ai/deskbot ──► composeTurn (tools = server ∪ advertised client actions)
                                            │
                     model step 1: desk_search_files  (server executes, result in stream)
                     model step 2: desk_open_file     (no execute — the call is streamed)
                                            ▼
browser: runner.run(call) ─ validate ─ handler ─ read the dock back ─► ClientActionResult
        addToolOutput(result) ─► same thread, POST /api/ai/deskbot again
                                            ▼
server: readClientActionResults ─ record on the trace ─ model step 3: the answer
```

Three states are kept apart, because merging them is how an agent reports work it never did:
**requested** (the call left the server), **executed** (a handler ran), **confirmed** (the
handler observed the intended state afterwards). Only `completed` means all three; `failed`,
`unavailable`, `refused` and `timed_out` each name the one that is missing.

## Component responsibilities

| Piece | Where | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| Catalogue | `#lib/types/ai-tools.ts` | Every action's name, risk, executor, scope, capability, result origin, reach |
| Client action contract | `#lib/client-actions/contract.ts` | `ClientActionContract` (name, input schema, timeout) and the bounded `ClientActionResult`. No framework, no SDK |
| Runner | `#lib/client-actions/runner.ts` | Registration with unmount, `available()`, and `run()`: unknown name, invalid input, missing handler, timeout, thrown handler, malformed result, duplicate call id. Never throws |
| The Desk's actions | `#lib/desk/arrange-actions.ts` | `desk_open_file`, `desk_focus_panel`, `desk_close_panel`: one declaration both sides read; the per-turn budget |
| Svelte adapter | `components/desk/arrange-action-handlers.ts` | The handlers: precondition against the live dock, act through the verbs a human gesture uses, read back, report |
| Server tools | `server/ai/tools/desk-arrange.ts` | The model-facing tools, derived from the same contracts, with no `execute` |
| Capability | `server/ai/capabilities/desk-arrange.ts` | When the actions are offered: scope granted, handler advertised, budget left; the guidance |
| Result reader | `server/ai/client-action-results.ts` | The one door a browser-produced result comes through before a model sees it |
| Session | `components/desk/panels/bot/desk-bot-session.svelte.ts` | Runs a call once, writes the result into the thread, decides whether the thread goes back |

## Decision record

**1. What it means here.** One way for the assistant to discover, understand, be authorized for
and coordinate application actions — not one way to implement them. A server tool and a client
action share a catalogue entry shape, a scope, a capability, a label, a trace record and a place
in the profile manifest; they do not share an execution mechanism, and should not.

**2. What already satisfied the requirement.**

| Requirement | Already there |
|---|---|
| Action catalogue with metadata | `TOOL_MANIFEST`, client-safe, read by the server, the UI and the admin pages |
| Discovery per turn | `AssistantProfile` → `AssistantCapability.activates` → `composeTurn`; the profile manifest |
| Authorization | Session auth in `guardAiRequest`; consent scopes (`DeskToolScope`); owner-scoped domain functions |
| Approval | `requiresApproval(risk)` → proposal → approve route → `executeDeskToolCall` → receipts → revert |
| Orchestration | One `chat-orchestrator.ts`, a multi-step agent loop, deadlines, fallback rotation |
| Evidence | The turn trace: every tool execution with its model-facing result |
| Untrusted results | `resultOrigin` / `reach`, `<untrusted-content>` wrapping in the turn and on replay |
| Server → UI consequences | `DeskEffect`: a server tool's result names what the desk should refresh or open |

**3. The gaps.** (a) No way for the model to *ask* the interface for something and learn whether
it happened — a `DeskEffect` is fire-and-forget and server-derived. (b) No risk tier for "changes
the view, not the data". (c) No notion of availability that depends on what is mounted in the
browser. (d) No reading of a tool result the server did not produce.

**4. Alternatives considered.**

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Server-held pending-action registry + a push channel (SSE) and a result endpoint | Needs cross-instance state and a session-routing table on a serverless deployment, plus a second transport and a second correlation scheme — for a result the open response stream already delivers to exactly the right browser |
| Extend `DeskEffect` with acknowledgements | Effects are consequences of a server tool, decided by the server. Giving them requests and results would make one name mean two things and still need the round trip |
| A separate frontend action registry beside the manifest | Two catalogues to keep in step, two permission surfaces, two sets of labels and trace records |
| Adopt the Vercel UI SDK agent runtime, or WebMCP | UI SDK was in beta and WebMCP in origin trial at decision time (2026-11); neither is consumed by the agent this app runs. Both map onto this contract as optional adapters — see [emulation](#emulating-it-elsewhere) |
| A workflow engine for cross-surface plans | The agent loop already orders steps and carries results; a client action adds one request boundary, not a new control structure |
| Generic commands (`click`, `eval`, a selector) | An unbounded action is not an action catalogue. Never accepted |

**5. Why this one.** It adds one field, one risk value, one scope and one capability to systems
that already exist, and one small framework-free module. The response stream of the turn is
already an authenticated, per-request channel to the one browser that asked; using it means
there is no session registry to get wrong, nothing to clean up when a tab closes, and no way
for a call to reach another user's browser. The AI SDK already supports tools without
`execute` — no dependency was added.

**6. How it avoids duplication.** Client actions are manifest entries, so the scope toggle, the
tool label, the admin tool matrix, the topology view, the profile manifest and the trace picked
them up from the catalogue. The action's input schema is declared once and read by the server
(model-facing schema) and the browser (validation before the handler). The handlers call the
same dock verbs as a click. There is no second orchestrator, permission system or execution
engine.

**7. Security, approvals and execution boundaries.**

- A client action can never change stored data. `client-actions.gate.test.ts` fails if a
  client-executed tool carries a risk an approval is owed for, appears among the tools the
  approval door replays, or lacks a contract; and if any server tool lacks an `execute`.
- Every write still goes through the approval gate, on the server, against the reviewed
  baseline. A client action result is never an input to an authorization decision: the only
  thing the server branches on is the action budget.
- A result is the user's browser describing the user's screen. It is declared
  `resultOrigin: 'user'`, read through the contract (anything else becomes
  `malformed_result`), bounded in size and shape, and wrapped as untrusted content for the
  model like every other user-origin result.
- The model supplies a file *id* only. The handler fetches the file's name and type from the
  owner-scoped route as the signed-in user, so an id the model was tricked into naming opens
  nothing that user could not open by hand.
- The agent gets less than the user: it cannot close the conversation it is speaking through,
  a panel that is not closable, or a panel with unsaved work.
- The client advertises which actions have a handler mounted *now* (`clientActions`, pinned to
  the declared names by the request schema); the server offers only advertised ∩ declared.
  Advertising is a consent-level fact, like the scopes: asserting it buys nothing, because the
  action still only runs in that same browser.
- Six client actions per user turn (`DESK_ARRANGE_MAX_ACTIONS_PER_TURN`); past it the
  capability deactivates and the model has to answer.

**8. Emulation.** See [Emulating it elsewhere](#emulating-it-elsewhere).

## Cross-surface behaviour

| Concern | What happens |
|---|---|
| Ordering and dependencies | The agent loop: the model reads a server result before it names a file id in a client action. No plan structure is added |
| Result propagation | The browser writes the result into the call's part; the continuation request carries the thread; `readClientActionResults` hands the last step's results to the orchestrator |
| Partial failure | A failed action is a result like any other; the model reports it. Earlier server work is not undone — reads have nothing to undo, writes were never run without approval |
| Cancellation | Stop aborts the stream. An action already running settles into the thread and the I/O log, and starts no new request |
| Retries and duplicates | The runner remembers call ids: a call delivered twice runs once. The session sends one continuation per settled step |
| Human approval | Unchanged. A turn that stops at the approval boundary is not continued by the client; only a step this session just settled is |
| Stale or closed browser | Unanswered calls are dropped from the history on the next request — no result, so nothing is claimed. A panel mid-remount gets 1.5 s for its handler to come back before the call is `unavailable` |
| Browser/server synchronisation | A continuation re-reads the desk (`turnBody()`), so the model sees the workspace the action left behind |
| Recovery | View changes need no compensation: the user closes the panel. Data changes keep the proposal's revert |

## Invariants

- Every agent action is a `TOOL_MANIFEST` entry with a declared `risk` and `executor`.
- A client-executed tool has risk `read` or `view`, no server `execute`, a declared contract,
  `resultOrigin: 'user'` and `reach: 'internal'`; it is never replayable by the approval door.
- A client action is offered only when its scope is granted, its handler is advertised by the
  requesting browser, and the turn's action budget is not spent.
- A handler answers `completed` only for a state it observed after acting.
- No client action result reaches a model unless it parsed as a `ClientActionResult`.
- The thread goes back to the server on its own only for a client action this session settled
  live — never for a step that ended on a server tool.
- Nothing accepts a script, a selector or a free-form command as an action.

## When to use it, and when not

Use a client action when the operation exists only in the interface (layout, focus, selection,
navigation, a viewport), the user could do it with a click, and undoing it is another click.

Do not use one for anything that changes stored data — make it a server tool so the approval
gate, the receipt and the revert apply. Do not use one when no user is watching (a job, an MCP
client): there is no browser to answer. Use a `DeskEffect` instead when the UI change is a
*consequence* of a server tool the model already called (refresh the file it just edited) and
the model does not need to know whether it happened.

## Emulating it elsewhere

1. Add `executor` to your tool catalogue and a risk tier for view-only changes. Gate the one
   forbidden combination — client-executed and data-changing — in a test.
2. Declare each client action once: name, input schema, timeout. Keep framework words out of
   the public input (files, panels, placements — not component refs or store keys).
3. Give the client a runner that never throws and always answers, and handlers that read back
   before they say `completed`.
4. Deliver calls on a channel that already ends in the right browser. With the AI SDK that is a
   tool without `execute`, `onToolCall`, `addToolOutput` and a `sendAutomaticallyWhen` you
   write yourself — the stock predicate also fires on steps that ended on a server tool.
5. On the server, read results through the contract before the model sees them, record them,
   and never branch an authorization on one.
6. Bound the round trips per user turn.

The contract does not depend on Svelte, the AI SDK, or a provider. A React adapter is another
set of handlers on the same runner. `document.modelContext.registerTool` (WebMCP) or a UI SDK
`createAgent` action list can be generated from the same contracts when an external agent
should see them; neither is needed for the in-app assistant, and neither is wired here.

## What is not claimed

- No live model run was recorded for this pattern in the session that built it (the cloud
  environment has no database or provider key). The proof is the unit and gate lanes listed
  below; the registry grades it `implemented`, not `proven`, until a browser-verified turn is.
- A turn with client actions spans two requests, so it is stored as two assistant rows and two
  traces: the first holds the server tools of the first request, the second the settled action
  and the answer. The thread shows one message; the inspector opens the latest trace.
- When the dock is already at its maximum depth, `placement: "right"` opens the file as a tab
  in the right-most pane rather than a new one, and reports `placed: "tab"`.
- Whether a model respects a non-`completed` status is guidance, not a guarantee; what the
  UI shows and what the trace records do not depend on it.

## Proof surface

| Concern | Test |
|---|---|
| Unknown action, invalid input, missing handler, timeout, thrown handler, malformed result, duplicates | `src/lib/client-actions/runner.test.ts` |
| Real dock: open / focus / close, refusals, read-back, another user's file id | `src/lib/components/desk/arrange-action-handlers.test.ts` |
| Executor × risk, approval door, `execute` presence, advertised names | `src/lib/server/ai/client-actions.gate.test.ts` |
| Forged, malformed, unanswered and errored results; budget count | `src/lib/server/ai/client-action-results.test.ts` |
| Continuation keeps the message id, records the result, budget, scope off, nothing advertised | `src/lib/server/ai/chat-orchestrator.test.ts` |
| Run once, continue once, never at the approval boundary, Stop, new chat, the cross-surface turn | `src/lib/components/desk/panels/bot/desk-bot-session.svelte.test.ts` |

Related: [surfaces.md](./surfaces.md) (the one door for mutations),
[untrusted-content.md](./untrusted-content.md) (result origin), [profiles.md](./profiles.md)
(capabilities), [../desk/README.md](../desk/README.md) (desk effects).

# Agent Skills — the pattern library as portable agent knowledge

**Maturity: built** (generated, gated in `validate`, and checked by the official validator).

## Problem

Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and ~70 other products)
load *Agent Skills* — folders with a `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + instructions) and optional
`references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`, disclosed progressively. v10r's knowledge already has a
canonical source, the pattern registry, projected into docs pages, MCP tools and the RAG
corpus. A hand-written set of skills would be a second body of knowledge that drifts.

## Decision

`skills/` at the repository root is a **generated surface** of `pattern-library/registry.json`:

| Agent skill | Contents |
|---|---|
| `v10r-architecture-selection` | How to choose patterns: the requirement vocabulary, `recommend_emulation_plan` / `get_pattern` / `search_patterns` over MCP, the by-hand method, the group table; `references/dependency-graph.md` (every `depends_on` edge in build order) |
| `v10r-<group>` × 7 (foundations, data, identity-safety, intelligence, features, velocity, integrity) | When to use, the method (avoid-when and alternatives first, then requires/depends-on, invariants as MUST-hold), a maturity legend (implemented ≠ proven; non-proven rows bold), the group's pattern index; `references/<id>.md` per deep record |

Granularity is one skill per registry **group**: every installed skill's description sits in
the agent's context permanently (8 ≈ cheap; 30 categories ≈ 6k tokens), a group is a domain an
agent recognises from a task, and per-pattern detail is disclosed on demand.

- Generator: `scripts/agent-skills/build.ts` (`skills:build`, `--check` as `skills:check` in
  `validate`; `skills:build` in `refresh`). Deterministic, orphan-cleaning, no timestamps.
  Rendering shares `patternBody` with the docs pages (`src/lib/server/patterns/render.ts`).
- Validator: `src/lib/server/patterns/agent-skill-spec.ts` — name rules and name = directory,
  description 1–1,024 chars, `compatibility` ≤ 500, `metadata` a string map, `allowed-tools`,
  unknown fields, body ≤ 500 lines and ≤ 5,000 tokens (errors, not warnings), broken relative
  links. `metadata`: `{ source, registry-version, generated: "true" }`; `license: MIT`.

## Sizes

| Agent skill | Lines | ~Tokens | References |
|---|---|---|---|
| v10r-architecture-selection | 39 | 820 | 1 |
| v10r-foundations | 130 | 4,367 | 13 |
| v10r-data | 43 | 1,098 | 0 |
| v10r-identity-safety | 55 | 1,452 | 1 |
| v10r-intelligence | 72 | 2,313 | 9 |
| v10r-features | 103 | 2,769 | 5 |
| v10r-velocity | 96 | 3,107 | 19 |
| v10r-integrity | 57 | 1,563 | 8 |

Tokens are chars/4 estimates. Foundations has ~12 % headroom; the gate fails when it outgrows it.

## Install

Two sources, one content. Both install the same bytes the registry renders.

| Source | Command | When |
|---|---|---|
| The repository | `npx skills add ApeDevil/v10r --skill v10r-architecture-selection` | Pinning a git ref (`ApeDevil/v10r@<sha>`); pass `--skill`, because the CLI also lists the repository's own development skills in `.claude/skills/` |
| A running v10r (discovery) | `npx skills add https://v10r.dev --skill v10r-intelligence -a claude-code` | No clone, no repository access, only the eight agent skills; digest-verified |

### Discovery endpoint

`/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` serves the Agent Skills discovery index, schema
0.2.0 (`src/lib/server/patterns/agent-skill-discovery.ts`, routes under
`src/routes/.well-known/agent-skills/`). Each entry is an `archive`: a deterministic
`.tar.gz` of one agent skill folder (SKILL.md plus `references/`) with a `sha256:` digest.

- **One source.** Built from `renderAgentSkills(REGISTRY)` once per server process, the same
  projection committed under `skills/` (the test asserts byte equality). Nothing is
  hand-maintained, and the hub `README.md` is not offered as an agent skill.
- **Integrity.** The installer downloads the archive, computes its digest and refuses on a
  mismatch before writing anything. It records the digest in `skills-lock.json`
  (`wellKnownDigest`), so `skills check` and `skills update` see content changes.
- **Stable digests.** mtime 0, uid/gid 0, fixed mode, registry order, gzip without a
  timestamp. The same registry gives the same bytes on every deployment.
- **Read-only and public.** `GET` only, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, one-hour cache, an
  unknown archive name is 404. It exposes exactly what the public repository's `skills/`
  already holds.
- **No promotion.** The archives carry the registry's maturity tags unchanged: an
  `experiment` or `implemented` pattern is marked bold as non-proven, as in `skills/`.

Not chosen: an npm package (a second release process for content the registry already
versions), per-file v0.1.0 entries (no integrity digest), and a Claude Code plugin
marketplace (one agent product only; the discovery index serves every agent the skills CLI
supports).

### Measured (2026-11-24, skills CLI 1.9.0, local dev server)

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Install | One command, about 10 s for two agent skills including `npx` resolution; files byte-identical to `skills/` |
| Resident context | All eight descriptions: 5,018 chars, about 1,250 tokens. Two installed: about 300 |
| Progressive disclosure | A body loads only when the agent picks the skill (≤ 4,400 tokens); a reference only when the body links it |
| Archive sizes | 2.4 KB (data) to 34 KB (foundations), 121 KB for all eight |
| Tampering | An archive with one appended byte: `SKILLS_WELLKNOWN_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, nothing installed |
| Updates | `skills check` against the source lists the six not yet installed agent skills; a changed archive changes its digest |
| Use in an external agent | Claude Code 2.1 in a fresh scratch project, after the install: it listed both v10r skills, opened `v10r-intelligence` and answered `ai-mcp-client` for consuming external MCP tools (3 turns) |

The production endpoint is not live until the branch ships; the measurements above are
against the local dev server.

## Validation

`agent-skill-discovery.test.ts` (every generated agent skill listed, archive round-trips to the committed files, digest matches, byte-deterministic, no hub README) and `agent-skills.test.ts` (committed tree = generated tree, valid, deterministic, one reference
per deep record, every pattern once, portable links) and `agent-skill-spec.test.ts` (bad
fixtures for every rule). The official `skills-ref validate` (Python, run once by hand)
reported all 8 valid.

## Not done

The MCP skills extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`, SEP-2640: `skills/list`,
`skills/get`, `skill://` resources) is not served — waiting for SDK support. The generated
skills are not ingested into the RAG corpus (it reads `docs/` only), so nothing is counted twice.
Found on the way: `.claude/skills/visy-diagram/SKILL.md` frontmatter is not valid YAML (an
unquoted `: ` in its description); both validators reject it and the skills CLI skips it.

# Agent to agent — A2A specialist agents

**Maturity: built** (server, client, assistant-driven delegation and a cross-language interop
run on branch work; delegation is wired to the deskbot through the external-operations
approval door — see Wiring; no live model turn has delegated yet; the official A2A TCK was not
run — see Validation).

## Problem

Some evaluations belong to agents another team, framework or language owns — a security
reviewer, a performance specialist, an infrastructure agent — deployed and versioned on their
own. v10r should be able to ask them, and to *be* one for others, without either side
adopting the other's runtime.

## When A2A, and when something simpler

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| A specialist inside the same app and runtime | A capability / sub-agent in the one orchestrator |
| A model that needs a tool | A tool (`TOOL_MANIFEST`), or MCP for someone else's tools |
| Two services you own, fixed contract | Direct service API (`external-service.md`) |
| An **independently operated agent** with its own lifecycle, long tasks, its own model and framework | **A2A** |

## Decision

- **Server.** `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and `POST /api/a2a` (JSON-RPC 1.0 binding, SSE
  streaming) over the official `@a2a-js/sdk` 1.3.0 — no Express: `http.adapter.ts` maps a web
  `Request` to the SDK's `JsonRpcTransportHandler`. Two skills: `architecture-security-review`
  and `architecture-review`, which run Architecture Studio's deterministic checks
  (`checkSecurity`, `checkArchitecture`) on a submitted model. **No model call, no quota, no
  user data.**
- **Per-request task store.** A fresh `DefaultRequestHandler` + `InMemoryTaskStore` per
  request: a shared store let `ListTasks` return other callers' tasks on a warm instance.
  Every task completes inside `execute`; earlier task ids answer `TaskNotFound`. Durable
  tasks would need a database `TaskStore` (not built; see AA11).
- **Bounded input.** Body ≤ model file limit + 64 KiB (413), ≤ 4 parts, text parts ≤ 2,000
  chars, exactly one data part (the model), `parseArchitectureModel` must pass; otherwise a
  `TASK_STATE_REJECTED` task with up to 50 issues. Public, unauthenticated, read-only, 30
  requests/min per /64 IP bucket, CSRF-exempt like the public MCP route.
- **Client.** `delegateArchitectureReview(peer, model, opts)`: exact-origin allowlist
  (`peer-policy.ts`); https, plain http only to a loopback IP literal when the caller passes
  `allowLoopbackHttp` (tests, interop); non-public addresses refused unless the peer lists an
  exact `PrivateDestination` (narrow CIDR + port; link-local never); one deadline; 512 KiB per
  response; JSON-RPC transport only, on the guarded fetch (the SDK's default factory would
  add a REST transport on the global fetch).
- **Secured transport, shared with MCP.** Every request goes through
  `server/http/peer-egress.ts` (`createPeerEgressFetch`) — see the next section.
- **Streaming and cancellation.** When the card offers streaming, the send is
  `SendStreamingMessage`: the first event names the remote task, so a timeout or abort after
  that point sends `CancelTask` on its own 3 s budget and records `cancellation`
  (`confirmed` · `not_confirmed` · `no_task`). A blocking peer returns no task id before its
  answer and cannot be cancelled. ≤ 64 stream events.
- **Claims, not evidence.** Every outcome is `claimed` · `declined` · `refused` and carries
  the literal `verified: false`, the remote `correlation` (task id, context id) and, for a
  refusal, `delivery` (`not_sent` · `sent` · `possibly_sent`). Findings are rebuilt from known
  fields; malformed entries are dropped and counted; a wrong envelope or > 200 findings
  refuses the whole report. The outgoing message carries `v10r.delegationDepth: 1`.

## Secured transport (shared with the MCP client)

One module holds the outbound responsibilities both protocols have, in this order per
request; each protocol keeps only its own policy and its own error vocabulary (`refuse`):

| Step | Held by `peer-egress.ts` | Protocol policy on top |
|---|---|---|
| Admission | asks `admit(url)` first; nothing is resolved before it | MCP: the peer's own origin only (`foreign_origin`). A2A: the allowlist, IP-literal check, scheme |
| Credential isolation | drops `cookie`, `authorization`, `proxy-authorization`; sends only `authorization()` | MCP: bearer by `MCP_PEER_SECRET_*`. A2A: bearer by `A2A_PEER_SECRET_*`, or none |
| Pinned connect | resolve once, every answer public or a listed `PrivateDestination`, socket to that address with SNI, certificate check and `Host` for the name (`pinned-fetch.ts`) | the `PrivateDestination`s the peer config lists |
| Redirects | a 3xx is a refusal | — |
| Size | declared `content-length` over the cap refused unread; the stream errors past the cap (SSE still streams) | MCP 4 MiB, A2A 512 KiB |
| Cancellation, timeouts | the egress signal merges with each request's own and reaches the socket | MCP: per-call timeout. A2A: one delegation deadline, separate cancel budget |

**Proxy restriction.** The pinned connect opens its own socket (`agent: false`) and ignores
`HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`: a forward proxy resolves the name again, which is
the second lookup pinning removes. A deployment whose only route out is an egress proxy
cannot reach MCP or A2A peers; the server functions need direct outbound TLS to each peer
address (Vercel functions have it). A proxy-only network needs a CONNECT-to-IP proxy and a
change in `peer-egress.ts`, not a setting. The interop harness's own probes (plain SDK
clients) still use the global fetch; product code never does.

## Assistant-driven delegation

`delegate_architecture_review` (manifest: chatbot, `risk: 'write'`, `reach: 'external'`,
`resultOrigin: 'user'`; capability `agent-delegation`) asks an operator-configured peer to
review an architecture model, through the external-operations contract
(`server/external-operations/contract.ts`):

1. **Peer authorization.** Only an `A2aDelegationPeer` the operator listed exists (id, label,
   origin, the A2A skills v10r may ask for, credential by secret reference, private
   destinations, reversibility). The model names a peer id, never an endpoint. A skill must be
   allowed by the operator *and* offered by the peer's card — the card can narrow, never widen.
2. **Budget and depth** (`createDelegationBudget`): one per turn, three per conversation,
   depth one — a turn that runs for a delegated task (none exists today) may not delegate.
   Spent before any network or human is involved.
3. **`prepare`** (adapter, `a2a/external-adapter.ts`): agent discovery — the card is read
   through the secured transport, no task sent — then the **disclosure** (destination origin,
   skill, the fields sent, a preview of the model, its size, the credential reference, `mutates:
   false`, the operator's reversibility, `grant: 'once'`) and the **binding** (card digest over
   name, version, interfaces, streaming and the chosen skill; operator policy digest;
   arguments digest; user; 10-minute expiry). The tool hands both to `propose` (the
   external-operations door) and answers the approval sentinel with the disclosure.
4. **`verify`** after approval: not expired, peer still listed with the same policy, card
   still digests the same.
5. **`execute`** once per approval, never retried: arguments must digest as approved; the
   delegation runs with the card digest bound, so a card swapped after `verify` refuses
   (`card_changed`) before the send. Outcome mapping: claim → `succeeded`/`sent`; declined →
   `failed`/`sent` (`peer_declined`); policy refusal → `refused`/`not_sent`; invalid answer or
   oversize → `failed`/`sent`; timeout or abort → `unknown`, or `failed` when the peer
   confirmed `CancelTask`. The result text is wrapped by the assistant layer's
   `wrapUntrusted`, and `remoteTask` carries the peer's task and context ids.

Requested, executed, claimed, confirmed, verified stay distinct: the receipt says the
operation was *requested* (approved) and *executed* (sent); `succeeded` means the peer
*claims* a completed review; a confirmed cancel is the peer's claim too; nothing a peer says
is ever *verified*.

### Wiring

Delegation is one more external operation, on the same path as an MCP peer tool
([external-operations.md](./external-operations.md)):

1. **Operator config.** `A2A_DELEGATION_PEERS` holds a JSON array of `A2aDelegationPeer`
   (`a2a/delegation-directory.ts`); an entry with a problem (`delegationPeerProblems`) is
   dropped with a warning. Secrets by reference only, `A2A_PEER_SECRET_*`
   (`a2aEnvironmentSecretResolver`). Unset: no peer, the capability stays inactive.
2. **Turn.** For a signed-in deskbot turn of a persisted conversation, the orchestrator builds
   the `DelegationTurnContext` (`delegationTurnContext`): the adapter, the peer choices, and a
   budget whose per-conversation count is read from the conversation's
   `agent_external_operation` rows (`countConversationExternalOperations`), so trimming the
   history a client sends does not reset it. The tool is in the manifest under the deskbot,
   `desk:read`, `risk: 'write'`, `reach: 'external'`.
3. **Propose.** The tool spends the budget, then `prepareExternalOperation` runs the content
   screen over what the turn read and the adapter's `prepare` (card read, no task sent), and
   stashes the prepared operation by tool call id. The orchestrator persists the proposal and
   its operation row in one transaction (`EXTERNAL_PROPOSAL_ALONE`: alone in its step); the
   `ExternalOperationCard` shows the disclosure.
4. **Execute.** The approve door's executor holds the `a2a` adapter
   (`externalOperationAdapters`): claim, `verify` (expiry, policy and card digest), dispatch
   marker, `execute` once, settle. The receipt records the remote task id (id-shaped values
   only; anything else is dropped, because the id is shown outside the untrusted wrapper) in
   the row's `result`, and the receipt message names it — the correlation key into the peer's
   own trace.

Evidence: `ai/proposals/a2a-delegation.pglite.test.ts` runs tool → proposal → two racing
executors against a loopback peer: one SendMessage on the wire, the remote task recorded, a
third executor answers from the row.

## Interoperability evidence

`bun run a2a:interop` (`scripts/a2a/interop-report.json`, byte-stable across runs): **24/24**.

- **JS client → Python server** (`scripts/a2a/peer/performance_agent.py`, Python `a2a-sdk`
  1.3.1 — an independently implemented performance specialist with its own rules): card,
  streamed claim with findings, adversarial reply (1 kept, 4 dropped), unknown skill and
  invalid model rejected, loopback refused without a listed private destination, unknown task
  get/cancel, streaming order.
- **Assistant delegation → Python server** (the adapter's prepare → verify → execute):
  success (wrapped, unverified claim with the remote task id), rejection (`peer_declined`),
  invalid report (`invalid_answer`, no claim), timeout and caller abort mid-task (both with a
  `CancelTask` the Python peer confirms as CANCELED), budget/depth refusal, a skill the card
  offers but the operator did not allow. Fixture skills exist only with `--allow-fixtures`.
- **Python client → v10r server** (the shipped adapter on `Bun.serve`): card at JSONRPC 1.0,
  security review completed, invalid model rejected, unknown task get/cancel, streaming.

## Security

Recursive delegation is bounded twice: v10r's served skills run deterministic checks, no
assistant, so an inbound task can never reach the delegation tool; and the delegation budget
refuses any proposal from a turn at depth ≥ 1. The tool is `reach: 'external'` and therefore
approval-gated (`untrusted-content.gate.test.ts`).

## Validation

`src/lib/server/a2a/*.test.ts` (65) and `src/lib/server/http/peer-egress.test.ts` (13), on real
loopback sockets through the pinned egress: card shape, send/stream, invalid model, oversized
body, unknown method, allowlist, SSRF (169.254.169.254, RFC 1918, unlisted loopback, the
metadata range even when listed), DNS rebinding between the card and the send, TLS name check
on a pinned address, redirect refusal, size cap (declared and streamed), abort, timeout with
and without a task to cancel, cancel confirmed and refused, malformed findings dropped and
counted, card drift, operator policy drift, expiry, tampered arguments, one execution per
approval, claims never verified. `src/lib/server/ai/tools/delegate-review.test.ts` (8): the
tool never executes, budget and depth, inactive without a context. **Not run:** `a2a-tck` (no
PyPI package; the GitHub download was blocked in the session) — run locally:
`git clone https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck && ./run_tck.py --sut-host http://localhost:5173/api/a2a`.

## Limitations

A2A 0.3 peers are refused (`legacyCompat` off; Mastra, ADK-TS and CrewAI still speak 0.3).
Agent Card JWS signatures are not used — the card digest pins what was approved, not who
signed it. No proxy support (see Secured transport). A blocking peer cannot be cancelled.
No live model turn has delegated yet (no provider keys in the cloud; the local procedure
covers it). The turn trace's `ToolExecutionRecord.remoteTask` is filled from the receipt row,
not from a column of its own on `ai.tool_call`.
